- [id: design: moderation pack format — data-only packs: static rules + feed subscriptions + parameters](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6005)
- [id: design: shared threat-list feed protocol — versioned, signed, subscribable feeds with local override lists](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6006)

Research source: `workspace/scratch/worlds-capabilities-brief-2026-11-04/prior-art-research.md`. Full wave-2 mapping: `workspace/scratch/worlds-capabilities-brief-2026-11-04/wave2-map.md`.

## Triage — task 10342 (lane code-s)

**Verdict: live design issue, correctly scoped, no Drew decision blocking. Stays OPEN as a design task; no code fix path.**

Evidence checked fresh 2026-11-05:

- Issue #5973 OPEN, no hard-stop labels (no held / user/owned / do-not-merge / do-not-auto-edit). Worlds program parent #5955 OPEN.

- Scope is coherent and non-duplicative as filed: #5861 is the board-surface hooks design; #5973 is the world-level generalization (moderation-as-library). The issue itself names the cross-pollinate-don't-duplicate boundary.

**Ordering / dependencies recorded:**
1. The moderation library's capability set presupposes the capability model in #5958 (triaged today, task 10327: vocabulary v1 + requested/used sets) — a moderation library "receives capabilities like any other code", so #5958's vocabulary should land first or be designed jointly.
2. Parameterization (moderator sets, report thresholds) rides on the KDL profile model #5753 — config-not-forks depends on that profile shape.
3. Pre-approval binding (content hash vs capability set) interacts with writer-set authority #5545; that interaction is an open design point on the issue, not a blocker.

No follow-up task enqueued — the design is this issue itself, already in the queue system via intake. Task 10342 completes as `triaged`.

- **next:** design doc in `doc/` + PR; this note supersedes the parked triage state.

```agent-note:v1
kind: progress
task: 12862
lane: bf419306-c4ef-470f-a553-beabf93239de
worker: repo-worker-code
at: 2026-11-08T13:42:30Z
status: pr_opened
artifact: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7708
```

Design record opened in PR #7708 (docs only, no code): `doc/2026-11-08T13-45-00Z_design_id_world_governance/`.

Settles the four deliverables — moderation-as-library interface (§2), the capability set a moderation library needs (§2.4), per-world parameterization (§4), pre-approval semantics (§5) — plus the authority model (§3) and the boards boundary (§6).

Two findings worth the issue owner's attention:

1. **The provider catalog has 13 entries and none is a moderation power**, and `RequiredScope` has no moderator variant. So governance actions are a `WorldCommand` family beside `Revoke`, not new providers. This is why §2.4's answer to "what capability set does a moderation library need" is "the same one a chat bot needs, and nothing more" — there is no `moderation.*` capability for a malicious pack to request that a benign one would not.
2. **Two same-named moderator notions exist in the substrate**: `WorldScopes::MODERATOR` (participant scope, admin-issued, revoke) and `Level::Moderator` (directory group level, gates isolation/cross-world/file-scope via `require_moderation`). §3.2 resolves them — directory level is the source, participant scope the grant — which is what lets a world host who is not a directory moderator still appoint world moderators.

**Packet drift recorded (§8):** this task's packet cites #5545 as live "writer-set authority"; #5545 is CLOSED (it was view projection, not authority). §3.3 corrects the reference to the writer-set design record + `membership/layer.rs`. Not blocking.

No implementation. Six slices are named in §9 for filing once the record is accepted. KDL serialization is deliberately not committed while #5753 is unlanded (§4.2).
